rationale: Imports are a tiny share of use and the domestic price is set by the world price at which Esker exports, so the tariff on a negligible import flow should not raise the domestic price by a substantial part of the tariff.
evidence: The domestic wheat price is set by the world price at which Esker exports.
Esker grows far more wheat than it uses and exports about half its harvest; imports were 0.1 percent of use last year, almost all of it a single specialty variety that domestic farms also grow.
